questions.q: What does the real ERC-2981 royaltyInfo(tokenId, salePrice) function return?
options: The current owner of the token only
A boolean indicating whether the sale is allowed
The full list of all past owners
The receiver address and the royalty amount owed for that sale price
questions.explain: royaltyInfo returns (address receiver, uint256 royaltyAmount) -- who should be paid and how much, for a given sale price.

questions.q: With salePrice = 10 ETH and feeNumerator = 500, what is the royalty amount per this lesson's worked example?
options: 5 ETH
0.5 ETH
0.05 ETH
50 ETH

questions.q: Why is ERC-2981 described as "a signal, not enforcement" in this lesson?
options: ERC-2981 automatically blocks any sale that doesn't pay the royalty
ERC-2981 has been deprecated and no longer functions at all
Nothing in the standard itself can stop a marketplace from settling a trade and simply ignoring royaltyInfo() entirely
Royalties are always paid in full by legal requirement
questions.explain: ERC-2981 communicates royalty terms, but marketplaces choose whether to honor them -- several major marketplaces have made royalties optional specifically because of this.

options: It overrides the contract-wide default royalty for one specific tokenId
It sets the royalty for every token in the contract at once, identically to _setDefaultRoyalty
It removes all royalties from the contract
It can only be called by the token's current owner, not the creator
questions.explain: _setTokenRoyalty lets a creator specify different royalty terms for one particular token, overriding the contract-wide default set by _setDefaultRoyalty.
